title.value: Balloon Dilation Techniques [source_page: 1; source_excerpt: 'Balloon Dilation Techniques']

diagnostic_approaches.name: Bronchoscopy (direct visualization)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Evaluate presence, degree, and extent of airway stenosis; assist in establishing underlying etiology
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Direct visualization via bronchoscopy; both flexible and rigid approaches apply.
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Best method for evaluating airway stenosis
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: the best method for evaluating the presence, degree, and extent of an airway stenosis is direct visualization via bronchoscopy.

diagnostic_approaches.name: Computed Tomography (CT) with reconstruction
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Assist diagnosis of airway stenosis as an ancillary study
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Better than standard radiographs or tomograms
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Ancillary study to assist evaluation when stenosis suspected
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: ancillary studies such as imaging (CT with reconstruction better than standard radiographs or tomograms), flow volume loops, and clinical exam.

diagnostic_approaches.name: Flow volume loops
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Assist diagnosis of airway stenosis as an ancillary study
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Ancillary study to assist evaluation when stenosis suspected
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: ancillary studies such as imaging (CT with reconstruction better than standard radiographs or tomograms), flow volume loops, and clinical exam.

diagnostic_approaches.name: Clinical exam (focal wheeze)
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Patients may have a focal wheeze on exam
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: When evaluating patients presenting with dyspnea
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Patients typically present with dyspnea and may have a focal wheeze on exam.

diagnostic_approaches.name: Symptom recurrence assessment
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Identify recurrent airway stenosis after prior treatment
criteria_or_scoring: Return of initial symptoms may indicate recurrence
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Return of initial symptoms may be a sign of recurrent stenosis
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: In patients with prior treatment for airway stenosis
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Return of initial symptoms, which may be slowly progressive in some instances, may be a sign of recurrent stenosis in those with prior treatment.

criteria_or_scoring: Inflammatory (i.e., sarcoidosis, eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis, and relapsing polychondritis)
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: For categorizing etiology in patients with airway stenosis

definitions.content: A nonconformal balloon is one that dilates to the desired conﬁguration and diameter without molding to the shape of the stenosis.
definitions.source_excerpt: A nonconformal balloon is one that dilates to the desired conﬁguration and diameter without molding to the shape of the stenosis.

clinical_pearls.content: A simple, safe, direct, inexpensive, repeatable, and rapidly effective option is balloon dilation, also called balloon bronchoplasty.
clinical_pearls.source_excerpt: A simple, safe, direct, inexpensive, repeatable, and rapidly effective option is balloon dilation, also called balloon bronchoplasty.

practice_recommendations.content: A high index of suspicion is required, and this may be assisted by ancillary studies such as imaging (CT with reconstruction better than standard radiographs or tomograms), ﬂow volume loops, and clinical exam.
